sources.name: LIDAR Composite Digital Terrain Model (DTM) - 1m
facts: ~99% England coverage
1 m spatial resolution
EPSG:27700
bare-earth DTM
vertical accuracy +/-15 cm RMSE
current catalogue page describes the 2022 composite using surveys from 2000-06-06 to 2022-04-02
limits: product publication/service availability does not prove a newer local survey
exact parcel raster sample remains required

sources.name: National LIDAR Programme
facts: 1 m national elevation programme
Phase 1 captured between 2017 and February 2023
repeat survey blocks are undertaken based on need
survey data is published quarterly on an ongoing basis
dataset period shown through 2023-05-05
limits: repeat-survey programme existence does not prove any of the three target points have newer coverage
exact spatial intersection is required before upgrading lineage

sources.name: LIDAR DTM Time Stamped Extents FeatureServer layer 0
facts: EPSG:27700 polygon layer
fields include sd_flown, ed_flown, pt_spacing, transform, geoid, latest and polygon_id
supported query formats JSON/geoJSON/PBF
Has Live Data=false
time extent shown 2005-2022
data last edit shown 2025-05-13
limits: schema/service availability is not an exact target intersection result

sources.name: Persistent WCS service update
facts: year-suffix composite endpoints were replaced with persistent endpoints
DTM1m WCS endpoint is documented with WCS 2.0.1
persistent endpoint is intended to avoid annual URL changes
limits: endpoint persistence does not itself prove underlying raster vintage at a target

sources.name: Survey Data Catalogue projection information
facts: EA survey data is supplied in OSGB36 British National Grid
elevations are above Ordnance Datum Newlyn
post-26-Aug-2016 surveys use OSGM15
time-stamped metadata should be consulted for the geoid model used by a specific survey
limits: datum model metadata is not terrain measurement accuracy

sources.name: INSPIRE July 2026 download
facts: dataset published 5 July 2026
new files published first Sunday each month
local-authority GML downloads
limits: monthly freshness does not make the polygons definitive legal boundaries

sources.name: INSPIRE Index Polygons catalogue
facts: last updated 8 July 2026
Open Government Licence
boundary-crossing polygons may appear in multiple local-authority files
limits: catalogue update date is provenance only

sources.name: INSPIRE GML technical guidance
facts: native coordinates use British National Grid
reprojection from BNG to WGS84 can shift some features by up to 15 m
limits: web-reprojected geometry cannot be promoted as exact native cadastral geometry

sources.name: Use Land and Property Data catalogue
facts: INSPIRE Index Polygons are updated monthly
catalogue states API available: No for INSPIRE
polygons show indicative position of registered freehold properties
limits: no official INSPIRE API should be invented
downloaded native GML remains the authority path

sources.name: National Geoid Model OSGM15
facts: converts ETRS89 ellipsoid height to orthometric height
mainland Britain output is ODN-compatible
1 km model grid with bilinear interpolation
nominal geoid-model accuracy 8 mm RMS in mainland UK
limits: 8 mm transformation-model accuracy must not be reported as LiDAR parcel-height accuracy

sources.name: Ordnance Datum Newlyn guidance
facts: ODN benchmark relative-error statistics are documented
OS warns benchmarks have not been maintained since the 1970s
subsidence of several metres has occurred in some mining areas
limits: legacy benchmark observations are not a substitute for current LiDAR target measurements

sources.name: OS Terrain 50 July 2026
facts: version date July 2026
coverage all Great Britain
OpenData/OGL
ASCII Grid available
limits: 50 m product remains secondary cross-check only for parcel-scale terrain
